messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Spike detected in EU-economy tier error rate and tail latency at 11:02 UTC. Affected routes: text.generate, embeddings.batch. Auto-mitigation candidates: tier-disable, regional-steer, rate-cap. Paging alice (oncall).
alice (oncall): ack, joining. pulling logs now.
jamie (runtime): I see a sudden rise in 5xx from the economy execution pool — kv-cache failures around the same time.
alice (oncall): local impact: 12% of EU requests hitting economy tier erroring, latency p99 up ~3s. Customer-facing incidents? sophia (support) do we have reports?
sophia (support): a handful of support tickets about timeouts on embeddings, 2 customers flagged increased latency. Not customer-wide yet.
rachel (sre): recommend immediate soft-mitigation: 1) raise economy per-customer rate cap by 20% for EU to reduce eviction storms 2) steer new economy traffic to eu-west2-b where capacity healthy 3) temporarily disable predictive-kv-cache prefetch for economy in EU. Thoughts?
alice (oncall): +1 for steering and kv-cache disable. raising caps could worsen evictions though — need to coordinate with platform.
mateo (platform): platform reports eu-west2-b has spare dedicated nodes, can accept a regional tilt. Will apply smart routing policy: route-policy "eu-economy-tilt-335000" shift 30% of new economy-lane traffic to eu-west2-b, prioritize latency-tier fallback for customers with SLA tag.
jamie (runtime): preparing hotpatch to disable predictive prefetch on economy-only pools. patch command:
```
service runtime update --pool=economy-eu --feature=prefetch --set=false --reason="mitigation 335000"
```
ops-bot: deploy queued to canary (eu-west2-b) — estimated apply 45s.
alice (oncall): applying steering now. mateo, pls post the policy command you run.
mateo (platform): running:
```
redwood-router set-policy --name eu-economy-tilt-335000 --match="tier:economy,region:EU" --split="eu-west2-b:0.30,eu-central:0.70" --priority=short_latency_fallback
```
ops-bot: policy applied to edge controllers. propagation in ~20s.
rachel (sre): jamie, once prefetch disabled, watch KV miss rates. If miss rate > 5% for 2 mins we should revert. Also add temporary rate-limit:
```
redwood-quota adjust --scope=pool:economy-eu --per-cust=+20% --temporary=15m --reason="mitigation 335000"
```
jamie (runtime): prefetch disabled on canary, rolling to 50% of economy-eu pools.
alice (oncall): monitoring dashboards: errors down to 6% (from 12%), p99 latency trending down. support — any new customer calls?
sophia (support): two follow-ups, both OK with us applying mitigations. One flagged they saw partial failures during 11:01-11:05.
rachel (sre): good. keep the tilt for 15m, then reassess. If steady, we can gradually re-enable prefetch on canary with stricter kv timeout.
mateo (platform): note: we also bumped dedicated-tier routing weight for paid SLA customers so they get prioritized lanes automatically. Command:
```
redwood-router weight-set --route=global --tag=SLA:paid --weight=1.25 --duration=20m --reason="protect paid traffic 335000"
```
alice (oncall): ops-bot, create incident-triage doc stub and ping #customer-notify if we escalate.
ops-bot: incident created: https://incidents.internal/3350001234. Notifying #customer-notify if severity upscales.
jamie (runtime): rolling metrics show kv miss spike but overall token throughput steady. 5xx reduced to baseline in canary.
rachel (sre): recommend keeping temporary quota bump and policy in place for 15 minutes, then revert quota and leave steering at 10% if stable. Also file postmortem to investigate why prefetch caused evictions.
alice (oncall): agreed. assigning postmortem to jamie + mateo + rachel. sophia, please collect affected customer list and any CS notes.
sophia (support): on it. I'll append tickets to incident doc.
alice (oncall): final check: do we want to fully disable economy predictive prefetch in EU for now? jamie:
jamie (runtime): not fully — keep disabled for 10m window, then enable on canary with reduced prefetch depth. I'll submit PR for config change.
alice (oncall): thanks team. keeping thread open for updates. mitigation window started 11:03 UTC, tentative rollback 11:18 UTC unless we see regression. :thumbsup:
